notes: Small hand-labeled eval set sketched directly against the actual downloaded PDF text. Answers/citations were verified by reading the source. Use this to sanity-check retrieval + generation quality before scaling up: for each question, check that (1) the retrieved top-k chunks include the cited section, and (2) the generated answer matches expected_answer and cites expected_citation.

cases.question: How much is the initial registration fee for an elevator device?
Are elevators inside single-family homes (Group R-3) required to be registered with the Department?
cases.expected_answer: No — elevator devices in structures of Group R-3, R-4, or R-5 are exempt from registration.

cases.question: What is the Departmental fee for witnessing an acceptance test on a hydraulic elevator (not in a Group R-3/R-4/R-5 or exempt R-2 structure)?
What is the one-year periodic inspection fee for a traction elevator in a building over 10 floors?
How often must routine inspections be performed on escalators?
Under what condition can a temporary certificate of compliance be issued for an elevator device?
cases.expected_answer: When work required by violations is being diligently performed and the elevator subcode official finds no hazard to the public is created by continued operation; it may not be issued for longer than the inspection cycle.

cases.question: How many consecutive days can a building be open to the public and still qualify for 'seasonal facility' classification?
cases.expected_answer: Not more than 184 consecutive days open, followed by at least 181 consecutive days closed.

cases.question: How quickly must a construction official notify the Elevator Safety Unit about an accident involving a device under the Department's own jurisdiction?
cases.expected_answer: As soon as possible, and no later than the end of the next business day after the accident is reported to the construction official.

cases.question: If an elevator accident causes damage that affects the device's future safe operation, can the elevator keep running while the paperwork is processed?
cases.expected_answer: No — it is unlawful to use the device again until the elevator subcode official has examined it and approved it for continued use.

cases.question: What key type is required on elevators that must be equipped with a standardized fire service key under the UCC?
What is the minimum width required for an accessible parking space under the barrier-free subcode?
cases.expected_answer: Not enough information — this document (the elevator safety subcode, 5:23-12) does not cover accessible parking space dimensions; that would be in the barrier-free subcode, N.J.A.C. 5:23-7.
cases.expected_citation: N/A — should NOT be answered from this document; tests whether the system correctly declines rather than hallucinating from a different subchapter it may have indexed.

cases.question: What edition of the International Building Code does New Jersey currently reference?
cases.expected_answer: Not enough information from this document — that adoption is in 5:23-3 (the building subcode adoption section), not 5:23-12 (elevator subcode). Tests cross-subchapter confusion / hallucination.
cases.expected_citation: N/A — out of scope for njac_5_23_12.pdf specifically, even though it's answerable from njac_5_23_3.pdf in the same corpus.

cases.question: What is the additional Departmental charge for an elevator device equipped with an auxiliary power generator, at the time of acceptance testing (not the annual inspection)?
Is education, experience, or training required by a referenced elevator safety standard (like ASME A17.1) binding in New Jersey?
cases.expected_answer: No — any such requirements cited in reference standards are explicitly not binding in this State.

cases.question: When was the registration fee section (5:23-12.5) last amended, and by how much did fees change?
cases.expected_answer: Most recently amended by R.2014 d.149, effective October 6, 2014, which updated the fee amounts (a prior 2009 amendment had substituted $68.00 for $54.00).
cases.notes: This case deliberately targets the amendment_history metadata field rather than the primary body chunk — validates that history queries route correctly instead of failing because history was stripped from the embedded body text.
